statements.text: Assessment: acute herpes zoster in a left L1 dermatomal distribution with associated pain; vesicular rash first noted 08/30/2026.
MRI thoracolumbar spine 08/26/2026: no compressive lesion; enhancement of the left L1 nerve root consistent with zoster radiculitis.
Function: unable to stand long enough to cook a meal, has stopped driving because of the pain.
Baseline VAS prior to any intervention: 63 mm.
Reports low back pain radiating to the left leg for 3 weeks.
Pain persists despite valacyclovir and gabapentin titrated to 900 mg daily; refractory to conservative management.
Remains engaged in a home exercise program five days a week.
Denies fever, chills, weight loss, or bowel or bladder changes; no history of cancer.
